question: How does a formula searched from measured joint firing change with length, and how does it compare qualitatively with the complete AND of its fixed parent formulas?

dataset.name: stanfordnlp/snli
dataset.order: Original capture row order. No resampling or held-out partition.
dataset.alignment_evidence: Parent search input hashes and capture replay. Raw activation tensors do not contain row identifiers.

search.target: AND of the two measured activation columns after strict > thresholding over all 10000 examples
search.length_definition: SymPy expression.count(Symbol), after automatic construction normalization

selection.rule: Select new layer-8 parents with an exact shared compound subtree before inspecting joint-search results. Use two longest five-atom shared compounds and one four-atom OR compound from a different expression family. Pairs have distinct neurons and nonzero measured joint support.
selection.exclusion_reason: No exact shared compound subtree in their new parent formulas.

outputs.symbolic_baseline: Evaluate each full parent formula over all examples and AND the results. Score only against measured joint firing.
outputs.sweep: Search measured joint firing at every listed maximum length. Independently evaluate and score each returned formula against that same measured target.
outputs.qualitative_assessment: Write a separate assessment of formula conditions and structure. Do not generate formula-to-formula agreement scores or automated conclusions.
